land.text: Sumer, Lugal-zage-si's kingdom, 'around 2300 BC, perhaps in 2292'

predecessors.note: Akkad itself rose at Kish's expense: Sargon 'usurped the kingship from Lugal-zage-si of Uruk and took it to his own city of Akkad'; the Kish page has Sargon as Ur-Zababa's cup-bearer (r. c. 2340).

land.text: Mari and the middle Euphrates, destroyed by Sargon c. 2290
'the Upper Land: Mari, Iarmuti, and Ebla'

predecessors.note: Ebla's first destruction (c. 2300) is attributed to Sargon by Matthiae and Bryce, to Mari by Archi and Biga, to a fire by Astour.

land.text: 'northern Babylonia around Akkad and Kish', the last Akkadian kingdom under Dudu and Shu-turul

successors.note: The Gutians held Adab and Umma earlier and took the Sumerian plain as Akkad shrank from 2189.

land.text: Lagash, Girsu and Nina, independent under Ur-Baba from c. 2164
Susiana, a vassal 'since the time of Sargon' until Elam 'claim[ed] independence' under Shar-kali-sharri

successors.note: Vassal tint, not direct territory, from c. 2290 to c. 2210.

capitals.name: Akkad (Agade)
capitals.note: 'Its location is still unknown'; drawn on the Tigris above Babylon, where most proposals place Agade. The coordinate is a placement, not a find.

rulers.name: Sargon
rulers.note: 'c. 2334–2279 BC in the middle chronology' (Sargon page); the king lists give 40 or 54–56 years.

rulers.name: Shar-kali-sharri
rulers.note: Came to power 'around 2217 BC (or 2205, or 2165 BC)', died 'around 2193 BC (or 2140 BC)'. The page lists no king for 2193–2189.

rulers.name: Dudu
rulers.note: 'a reduced kingdom, likely limited to northern Babylonia around Akkad and Kish'.

rulers.name: Shu-turul
rulers.note: 'known only from a handful of votive inscriptions'.

correction.text: Akkad and Kish, the northern Babylonia of Sargon's own city: he 'usurped the kingship from Lugal-zage-si of Uruk and took it to his own city of Akkad'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the infobox founds the empire c. 2334 but Cliopatria's first shape starts -2300, when Sumer was taken ('around 2300 BC, perhaps in 2292'). Sargon's conquests ran 'c. 2340 to c. 2284' (infobox); until Sumer fell the state is drawn on Akkad.

390,387 km2 for -2300..-2251: 'most of Mesopotamia and parts of the Levant, Hurrian and Elamite territory'; 'the Upper Land: Mari, Iarmuti, and Ebla' up to 'the Cedar Forest (and) up to the Silver Mountain' (bbox to 35.3 E, 37.8 N). No infobox area to compare. Susa and Warahshe 'became vassals of Akkad': the Iranian part should take the vassal tint (ledger -2290), not the full colour. [fixer me-01: ok -> adjust, Khuzestan (70 cells of the shape) removed so that Susiana is not claimed twice; the vassalage is the ledger's from -2290.]

correction.text: Sargon's empire without Susiana: Elam holds Khuzestan throughout (elam_-2700) and Akkad's lordship over Susa and Warahshe is a vassal tint (ledger -2290..-2210), not direct territory as Cliopatria draws it

Naram-Sin's empire from the Upper Sea to the Lower Sea, Upper Mesopotamia and northern Syria (a stele at Pir Hüseyin near Diyarbakır) included, without Magan: Manishtushu 'claimed to have subjugated Magan after sending ships across the Persian Gulf' and Naram-Sin 'is said to have subjugated Magan'; campaigns, not held land. Without Khuzestan (Elam's vassal land, ledger). Anshan (the Fars core) is held for -2250..-2241 only: 'The 3rd ruler, Manishtushu, conquered the city of Anshan in Elam' (Naram-Sin page), lost to Elam in -2240

keyframe_review.note: 526,585 km2 for -2250..-2201, the peak (bbox 32.5–56.5 E, 24.5–37.9 N): Oman is removed (10 cells) and Khuzestan is removed (221 cells, Elam's vassal land). The Persis plateau part of the shape (104 cells, the Anshan core, Fars and Bushehr; the bbox's 56.5 E is Gulf coast in the Emirates) is kept for -2250..-2241: the Akkadian Empire page says Manishtushu 'led campaigns into the Iranian Plateau (against Anshan, Sherihum)' and 'conquered Ansan and Sirihum', the Naram-Sin page that he 'conquered the city of Anshan in Elam', and the Elam page that Kutik-Inshushinak 'conquered Susa and Anshan' (c. 2240–2220), which presupposes Anshan was not Elam's. Disagreement: the Awan dynasty page says 'The capital of Anshan, located in a steep and mountainous area, was never reached by Akkad'; the conquest reading is used (three pages, and Cliopatria's own shape) and the Awan page is noted. From -2240 see akkadian-empire_-2240. Marhashi (Sargon 'claimed victory over Elam, and also over Marhashi') is not drawn. Years right: Naram-Sin r. c. 2255–2218. [fixer me-01: the first version kept the plateau without an event; now explained by the gain -2255 and the loss -2240.] This keyframe holds -2250..-2241.

correction.text: The -2250 peak without Magan, Khuzestan and, after Kutik-Inshushinak 'conquered Susa and Anshan' (Elam page, c. 2240-2220), without Anshan

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the peak shape from the loss of Anshan to Elam (ledger -2240) to the loss of Adab (-2220). Cliopatria's -2200 shape no longer reaches the Fars plateau (0 cells of Persis), which agrees.

correction.text: The -2250 peak without Magan, Khuzestan, Anshan and Adab, which the Gutians occupied: 'By the end of the Akkadian period, the Sumerian city of Adab was occupied by the Gutians, who made it their capital'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe from the Gutian foundation (infobox 'Established: c. 2220 BC'); settles the double claim over Adab that the Gutian dossier's found event flagged (-2220..-2190).

correction.text: Shar-kali-sharri's shrinking empire without Susiana, where Akkad's weakness allowed 'Elam to claim independence' (Kutik-Inshushinak page), and without Adab, held by the Gutians; from Dudu (2189) only 'northern Babylonia around Akkad and Kish' remained, and the dynasty ended c. 2154: the shape's years are -2200..-2154, not -2101

keyframe_review.note: 296,576 km2 for -2200..-2101: the end year is wrong by 47 years ('Disestablished: c. 2154 BC'; Shu-turul 2168–2154); -2153..-2101 belong to the Gutians, Lagash, Uruk and Ur III. The ledger's -2189 and -2164 losses shrink it to Akkad before the end. [fixer me-01: Adab removed to agree with the Gutian found event and the loss -2220.]

ledger.note: 2334 BCE: Sargon founds the kingdom of Akkad. Infobox 'Established: c. 2334 BC'; his reign 'c. 2334–2279 BC in the middle chronology'; capital Akkad, 'Its location is still unknown'. Sargon 'usurped the kingship from Lugal-zage-si of Uruk and took it to his own city of Akkad'.

region.text: Lower Mesopotamia: Uruk, Ur, Lagash 'to the sea', Umma

ledger.note: 2300 BCE: Sargon conquers Sumer. He defeated Lugal-zage-si 'around 2300 BC, perhaps in 2292', 'bringing Lower Mesopotamia under his control'; the Sargon page: he 'defeated the city of Uruk and tore down its walls' and 'was victorious over Ur in battle'.

region.text: 'the Upper Land: Mari, Iarmuti, and Ebla' up to 'the Cedar Forest (and) up to the Silver Mountain'

ledger.note: 2300 BCE: Ebla's first kingdom falls; Sargon claims the Upper Land. The Ebla page dates the burning of palace G c. 2300 BC and names Sargon as the destroyer for Matthiae and Bryce, Mari for Archi and Biga, a natural fire (c. 2290) for Astour; Sargon's own inscription is undated. The attribution is the gap.

2290 BCE: Sargon destroys Mari. 'Just a decade after Ebla's destruction (c. 2300 BC middle chronology), Mari itself was destroyed and burned by' Sargon; Astour's short chronology gives c. 2265. Mari was 'deserted for two generations' until Manishtushu restored it and appointed a Shakkanakku (Ididish, c. 2266).

region.text: 'the governors, viceroys, and kings of Susa, Waraḫše, and neighboring districts became vassals of Akkad'

ledger.note: 2290 BCE: Susa and Warahshe become Akkad's vassals. 'In the east, Sargon defeated four leaders of Elam, led by the king of Awan' (Luh-ishan, d. c. 2325 on the Awan page); undated within the reign, placed with the other conquests. Lighter tint (rule 4), not direct territory as Cliopatria draws it. Re-read for the fixer: the Sargon page has 'the governors, viceroys, and kings of Susa, Waraḫše, and neighboring districts became vassals of Akkad' (no date), the Awan dynasty page 'the low-lying, westerly parts of Elam became a vassal of Akkad, centred at Susa', the Naram-Sin page 'Naram-Sin exercised great influence over Susa during his reign'; elam now carries the mirror.

region.text: the cities of Sumer in revolt under Kaku of Ur

ledger.note: 2279 BCE: Rimush faces a Sumerian revolt. 'He put down a revolt led by Kaku of Ur'; 'His inscriptions record heavy casualties in Sumer'. Rimush r. 2279–2270; the revolt's years are not on the page, so it is drawn for his accession year only.
2278 BCE: the revolt is crushed. Bridged; the page gives no end year.

region.text: Anshan (the Fars core): Manishtushu 'conquered Ansan and Sirihum'

ledger.note: 2255 BCE: Manishtushu takes Anshan. The page: 'During his fifteen-year reign, Manishtushu also led campaigns into the Iranian Plateau (against Anshan, Sherihum)'; his inscription says he 'conquered Ansan and Sirihum'; the Naram-Sin page: 'The 3rd ruler, Manishtushu, conquered the city of Anshan in Elam'. No page gives a year inside his reign (c. 2270–2255); placed at its end, the last year before Cliopatria's -2250 shape first shows the Fars plateau (104 cells). A king's claim, so confidence 1; the land is the Anshan core that elam_-2200 draws. The Awan dynasty page disagrees ('The capital of Anshan ... was never reached by Akkad').

region.text: Kish's northern coalition and the cities of Sumer in the Great Revolt

ledger.note: 2254 BCE: the Great Revolt against Naram-Sin. Iphur-Kish 'r. c. 2254 BC' 'led a northern coalition during the Great Revolt against Naram-Suen'; the Akkad page: 'At some unspecified point during his reign'. Start and end are the accession year; the revolt's length is not on the pages. Re-read for the fixer: the Naram-Sin page says only 'At some point in his reign a widespread uprising occurred, a large coalition of city-states led by Iphur-Kis' and gives neither a date nor a length.
2253 BCE: Naram-Sin crushes the Great Revolt. Bridged end year.

region.text: northern Syria to the coast: Naram-Sin's 'campaigns reached Upper Mesopotamia and northern Syria' and his inscription 'claims the conquest of Armanum and Ebla'

ledger.note: 2250 BCE: Naram-Sin reaches the Mediterranean. Cliopatria's -2250 shape adds the Syrian coast (bbox west 32.5 E); the Ebla page gives Naram-Sin's Armanum-and-Ebla claim without a date, the Akkad page his accession c. 2254. Year bridged; Ebla's second kingdom (c. 2300–2000) has no dossier yet.

2240 BCE: Anshan passes to Elam. 'Elam declared independence under the last Awan king, Kutik-Inshushinak (c. 2240 – c. 2220 BC)' and 'conquered Susa and Anshan' (Elam page; long chronology: the Kutik-Inshushinak page overlaps him with Ur-Nammu); the Awan dynasty page: 'When the Akkadian empire started to break down around 2240 BC, it was Kutik-Inshushinak ... who liberated Awan and Elam'. Mirror of elam /ledger (gain of Persis, -2240). Susa itself stays a vassal until -2210 (ledger), the Akkad dossier's own bridge.

2220 BCE: the Gutians hold Adab. 'By the end of the Akkadian period, the Sumerian city of Adab was occupied by the Gutians, who made it their capital' (infobox 'Established: c. 2220 BC'); the Akkadian Empire page: they 'ultimately settle in the vicinity of Adab'. The year is the Gutian dossier's founding year; the page gives no date for the loss itself. Mirror of gutian-dynasty /ledger/0 (found).

2210 BCE: Elam breaks free. 'Under Shar-Kali-Sharri, Akkad weakened, allowing Elam to claim independence'; Kutik-Inshushinak 'conquered Susa and Anshan' (Elam page: c. 2240–2220, a long chronology; his own page has him overlap Ur-Nammu, 2112–2094). Placed in Shar-kali-sharri's reign (2218–2193); the chronology conflict is the gap.

region.text: Sumer apart from Lagash: Dudu 'held a reduced kingdom, likely limited to northern Babylonia around Akkad and Kish'

ledger.note: 2189 BCE: Akkad shrinks to Akkad and Kish. Dudu (2189–2168) is 'known from votive inscriptions and references to campaigns'; the Gutians 'settled near Adab', 'made it their capital' and held governors at Umma (Gutian page); Uruk's fourth dynasty follows in 2154. The counterpart is the Gutians as the largest holder; the year is Dudu's accession. [fixer me-01: region unchanged, now matched by gutian-dynasty's gain (Sumer apart from Lagash, Uruk included); Uruk goes to its own dynasty from the Gutians in -2154.]

2164 BCE: Lagash is independent under Ur-Baba. Puzur-Mama, governor under Shar-kali-sharri, 'later declared Lagash independent, though Dudu of Akkad still reported taking booty from there'; Ur-Baba 'r. c. 2164 – c. 2144 BC' opens the Second Dynasty.

2154 BCE: the Akkadian dynasty ends. 'Disestablished: c. 2154 BC'; Shu-turul (2168–2154) 'is known only from a handful of votive inscriptions'; the fall was gradual, 'with drought and the 4.2-kiloyear event contributing', the Gutians raiding 'in the final decades'. The Gutian period follows (c. 2154–2119).

wars.name: Sargon's conquests

zones.text: the Upper Land to the Cedar Forest and the Silver Mountain

wars.outcome: Infobox 'Conquests of Sargon of Akkad: c. 2340 to c. 2284 BC': Sumer annexed, Mari destroyed, the Upper Land claimed, Elam's leaders defeated and Susa made a vassal; the empire 'is thought to have included most of Mesopotamia and parts of the Levant, Hurrian and Elamite territory'.
wars.note: 'Afterward in his old age all the lands revolted against him, and they besieged him in Akkad' (undated).

wars.name: Rimush's campaigns
wars.outcome: The revolt of Kaku of Ur crushed with 'heavy casualties in Sumer'; campaigns 'against Elam, Awan, and Marhashi' (Emahsini defeated, Awan page). No border moved.

wars.name: Manishtushu's campaigns
wars.outcome: 'campaigned against Anshan and Sherihum on the Iranian Plateau and claimed to have subjugated Magan after sending ships across the Persian Gulf'; Mari restored under a Shakkanakku (c. 2266). Campaign reaches, not territory.

wars.name: Great Revolt against Naram-Sin

zones.text: the northern coalition under Kish and the cities of Sumer

wars.outcome: Suppressed; Naram-Sin's reign went on to its peak. Dates bridged from Iphur-Kish 'r. c. 2254 BC'.

wars.name: Naram-Sin's campaigns
wars.outcome: 'His campaigns reached Upper Mesopotamia and northern Syria' (stele at Pir Hüseyin near Diyarbakır); Armanum and Ebla claimed; Magan 'said to have' been subjugated; a treaty with Awan (Khita or Helu).

wars.name: Gutian war and the fall of Akkad

zones.text: the Sumerian plain, lost to the Gutians, Lagash and Uruk

wars.outcome: 'The Gutians raided Mesopotamia in the final decades, and some settled near Adab'; Akkad shrank to 'northern Babylonia around Akkad and Kish' and ended c. 2154. The page treats 'the Gutian blame as less certain today' beside drought and the 4.2-kiloyear event.

certainty.note: No surveyed line: the Sumerian core follows the city territories, the Upper Land, Elamite and Gulf claims are campaign reaches; the Diyala and Zagros edge is a march.

notes:
Cliopatria's three shapes (-2300, -2250, -2200) are kept with three corrections: a new keyframe -2334..-2301 on Akkad (the infobox's founding date precedes the first shape by 34 years), Magan (Oman) and Khuzestan removed from the -2250 peak, Khuzestan removed from the -2300 and -2200 shapes and its end moved from -2101 to -2154 (the infobox's disestablishment). No infobox area exists, so Cliopatria's 527,000 km2 peak is unchecked; it is plausible for 'from the Upper Sea to the Lower Sea' once Oman is dropped.

Vassals: the Sargon page makes Susa and Warahshe vassals 'of Akkad'; the Kutik-Inshushinak page: 'Elam had been a vassal of Akkad since the time of Sargon'. Drawn as vassal tint -2290..-2210 (both years bridged). The pages disagree by a century on Kutik-Inshushinak (c. 2240–2220 long chronology on the Elam and Awan pages; contemporary of Ur-Nammu 2112–2094 on his own); this dossier ends the vassalage under Shar-kali-sharri as the Kutik page says, and the Elam dossier keeps his Susa-and-Anshan union at -2240 with the conflict noted.

Rebellions (rule 5): Kaku of Ur's revolt under Rimush and the Great Revolt under Naram-Sin are recorded as contests of one year each at confidence 1; no page gives their length. No rebel dossier was written for them.

Counterparts without dossiers: 'Ebla (second kingdom)' (c. 2300–2000), Marhashi, Anshan before Elam's union, Magan, Lullubi, Armanum. Eshnunna and Akshak appear in the Kutik page as Elamite conquests c. 2110, after this state's end.

Page budget: 2 of 2 (Akkadian Empire, Sargon of Akkad); the other cited pages were opened for neighbouring dossiers of this batch. Naram-Sin's own page was not opened: the Great Revolt's length and the dates of Armanum and Ebla remain gaps.

ME-01 FIXES (after the review): (1) Khuzestan is no longer drawn as Akkad's land in any shape (Elam holds it, vassal tint from the ledger -2290..-2210, now mirrored in elam). (2) The Fars reach of the -2250 peak (104 cells of the Persis plateau, the Anshan core; the bbox to 56.5 E is mostly Gulf coast) is now explained: gain -2255 (Manishtushu 'conquered Ansan and Sirihum', Akkadian Empire page; 'conquered the city of Anshan in Elam', Naram-Sin page; confidence 1, the year being the end of his reign) and loss -2240 to Elam (Kutik-Inshushinak 'conquered Susa and Anshan', Elam page), mirrored in elam; keyframes akkadian-empire_-2240 and _-2220 draw the later years, and Cliopatria's -2200 shape indeed has no Persis cells. The Awan dynasty page says 'The capital of Anshan ... was never reached by Akkad': pages disagree, and the alternative (drop the plateau, keep elam's gain from nobody) was the reviewer's other option. (3) Adab is lost to the Gutians in -2220 (mirror of the Gutian found); _-2220 and _-2200 exclude it; _-2250 now holds -2250..-2241. (4) The Gutian gain of -2189 now covers Uruk as this dossier's loss does. Thin items: the Naram-Sin page (opened) dates neither the Great Revolt, its length, Kaku's revolt nor the Amarnum/Ebla campaign, so those stay at confidence 1; Rimush's page was not opened. Chronology: the Awan page puts Akkad's breakdown and Kutik-Inshushinak's liberation 'around 2240 BC'; the vassal end here stays at -2210 (Shar-kali-sharri), the original bridge.

RIMUSH PAGE (me-01 fixer): it says Elam 'would be ruled by Akkadian Military Governors, starting with Eshpum', and has Rimush reconquering 'the cities of Ur, Umma, Adab, Lagash, Der, KI.ANki, and Kazallu from rebellious ensis' (no revolt length, no name Kaku, one year-name 'year in which Adab was destroyed'): the Kaku revolt stays a one-year contest at confidence 1 and Susiana may have been governed directly rather than as a vassal state (the vassal tint is kept, see elam notes).
